paragraphs: A Mercedes-Benz M152 engine rebuild starts from £3,600, regardless of which of the six models it's fitted to - the price tier is set by the engine, not the badge on the boot. A full replacement engine and fitting service is also available.
Exact pricing depends on the condition of your existing engine and the parts required - submit your registration for a fixed-price quote within 30 minutes.

cards.title: Rebuilding Your
cards.body: Most engine suppliers sell you a used engine of unknown history and hope it matches. We rebuild the engine your Mercedes already has instead - strip it down, pressure-test it, and replace every worn or damaged component with updated OEM parts. You get a near-new engine with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty, without the compatibility risk of an unknown used unit. This is the option most M152 owners choose.

cards.title: Replacement
cards.body: If your existing engine is beyond economical repair, we also offer full engine replacement and fitting - sourced and fitted by our team, with the same 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

cards.title: Used
cards.body: In some cases, a matched low-mileage used engine is the right call - particularly if you need your car back on the road quickly and your existing engine's damage is extensive. We can source and fit these too, though most owners who ask about used engines end up choosing a rebuild once they understand the compatibility risk a used unit carries.

options.body: "Reconditioned" is the term many owners search for when they mean the same thing as a rebuild - a full strip-down, inspection, and replacement of worn parts rather than a straight swap. If that's what you're after, our rebuild service is exactly that.
"Refurbished" often describes the same process from a different angle - restoring your existing engine to full working condition rather than replacing it outright. Our rebuild covers this.

Some owners specifically search for a "remanufactured" engine, expecting a unit rebuilt to original specification with updated components. That's consistent with what our rebuild service delivers, regardless of which of the six M152-equipped models you drive.

faqLeft.q: What is the Mercedes-Benz M152 engine?
faqLeft.a: The M152 is AMG's naturally aspirated 5.5-litre V8 petrol engine, produced from 2004 to 2011 and fitted exclusively to the SLK 55 AMG (R171 generation).

faqLeft.q: Which Mercedes models use the M152?
faqLeft.a: Only the SLK 55 AMG (R171, 2004-2011). No other Mercedes-Benz model carries this specific engine code.

faqLeft.q: Does the M152 differ between Mercedes models?
faqLeft.a: No - the M152 was fitted exclusively to the SLK 55 AMG, so there's only one application.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes-Benz M152 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £5,500, reflecting the AMG V8 tier. Exact price depends on condition and parts required - submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.
Yes. We work on M152 rebuilds for the SLK 55 AMG, replacing timing chains, bearings, and gaskets as standard.

faqRight.q: What are common M152 engine issues?
faqRight.a: Oil consumption, rear main seal leaks, and vibration damper/pulley wear are documented patterns. We address these during a full rebuild.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Mercedes-Benz M152 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Mercedes if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes - nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an M152 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most M152 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.
